sub_scenario.family: rehearsal load versus protected voice clarity
sub_scenario.one_line: podcast production editor: reject the live reads; provide time-coded notes and one short check-in

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the episode rundown and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The recording calendar review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can edit interviews silently for a full afternoon.
That is preparation without voice load.
It leaves me fresh for recording.
Someone new shadowed me in the audio booth this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the launch weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On 6 April, I prepared the science-series pilot with time-coded notes, then chaired one 45-minute table read.
How did your launch recording go?
My narration was clean at the 09:00 session the next morning.
I can send hosts time-coded notes instead of talking through every transition.
Would that replace a table read?
Yes, the host can mark changes independently.
I archived last cycle's notes on the recording calendar and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
You sometimes join a long dinner conversation.
I do, but I do not narrate continuously or work in a dry booth afterward.
Social talk does not test the same thing.
A vendor call about the episode rundown ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the audio booth checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the launch weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the recording calendar records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On 16 June, I hosted two evening table reads and a pickup session before a 09:00 sponsor recording.
What was the consequence?
I lost the upper range on the sponsor copy and we postponed the session.
I sketched next week's plan for the launch weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the episode rundown updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
I am recovering from a sinus infection, and the audiologist asked me to avoid extended talking while congestion clears.
Can you still prepare the episode?
Yes, through edits and time-coded notes.
A host says both table reads would make me look fully committed to the new series.
Does that alter the sponsor's booked recording?
No, the sponsor and studio are fixed for Friday morning.
I closed the week by updating the audio booth handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Should I schedule two Thursday evening table reads before the sponsor recording Friday at 09:00?
